transcript.answer: At most three upkeep runs can start per repository for one event (a push to main). The pull requests that go first are the ones upkept longest ago. Order: a pull request never upkept comes first, then the one whose newest upkeep run started earliest, then the oldest pull request. This rule was added 2026-10-25 (FR12.19a). Before it, the three oldest pull requests always got the starts. When those three kept failing, they took every start on every push and starved the rest. Pull requests left over wait for the next event. Upkeep also only starts for open loop pull requests (branch `lore/implementation-loop/issue-<n>`) that GitHub calls behind main, under a branch rule asking for up to date. Pull requests whose ticket the loop parked with `lore:blocked` are skipped.

judgements.reason: The answer states the cap of three per event per repository and the full longest-ago-upkept ordering (never upkept, then earliest newest upkeep run, then oldest), with extra detail that does not contradict the gold.
